Description

Executive Director

Congregation Shomrei Torah (CST)

Santa Rosa, California | Full-Time | Exempt

Salary:
$120,000–$140,000

Help Shape the Future of Reform Jewish Life in Sonoma County

Congregation Shomrei Torah (CST), a vibrant, nearly 500-family Union for Reform Judaism (URJ)-affiliated synagogue, is seeking an entrepreneurial, relationship-centered Executive Director to help lead our community into its next chapter.

Our next Executive Director will partner closely with our Senior Rabbi, Jeremy Morrison; our Board of Directors; professional staff; and congregants to strengthen our visibility throughout Sonoma County, deepen member engagement, cultivate philanthropy, develop future leaders, and help shape a thriving, values-driven Jewish community.

Operations are supported by an experienced administrative and operations team, allowing this position to focus on strategic leadership, relationships, organizational growth, and community impact.

If you are energized by building organizations, cultivating relationships, mentoring staff, and helping communities live their mission, we'd love to hear from you.

Position Overview

Reporting to the Senior Rabbi and working closely with the President of the Board of Directors, the Executive Director serves as the congregation's chief administrative and strategic partner.

Success in this role is measured not simply by keeping the synagogue running smoothly, but by helping Congregation Shomrei Torah become an increasingly visible, connected, and engaged Jewish community.

The Executive Director will strengthen organizational capacity, expand community relationships, oversee administrative operations, supervise staff, and help build systems that support meaningful lifelong Jewish engagement.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Partner with the Senior Rabbi and Board to articulate and execute the congregation's long-term strategic vision.
Translate organizational priorities into measurable initiatives.
Serve as a trusted advisor to clergy and lay leadership.
Help align staff, volunteers, committees, and leadership around shared goals.

Membership Engagement & Leadership Development

Lead The Congregation's Efforts To Create a Relationship-centered Culture Where Members Build Meaningful Connections, Deepen Their Engagement With Jewish Life, And Grow As Active Participants And Leaders Within The Community By

Building authentic relationships with current and prospective members.
Designing and implementing a relationship-centered membership engagement strategy.
Create and oversee a relationship-centered member engagement system that tracks individuals throughout their synagogue journey, using personalized touchpoints and data-informed relationship management to deepen connection, foster belonging, and strengthen member recruitment, engagement, and retention.
Partnering with clergy, staff, and volunteer leaders to cultivate the next generation of synagogue leadership.
Supporting committee chairs and volunteer leaders in building collaborative, mission-driven teams that advance the congregation's vision.

Communications & Public Presence

Help ensure CST becomes a well-known and welcoming Jewish home throughout Sonoma County by:

Developing and implementing a comprehensive communications strategy.
Strengthening storytelling, marketing, and social media.
Clearly communicating the congregation's identity and mission.
Serving as one of the synagogue's public ambassadors within the broader community.

Community Partnerships

Develop meaningful relationships with organizations whose work advances the congregation's mission, including:

Civic organizations
Educational institutions
Social justice organizations
Jewish communal partners
Community leaders and philanthropic organizations

Development & Philanthropy

Support a Culture Of Generosity By

Cultivating donor relationships.
Identifying and pursuing grant opportunities.
Supporting fundraising campaigns and special initiatives.
Partnering with clergy and volunteer leadership on donor stewardship.
Exploring innovative revenue opportunities aligned with the congregation's mission.

Staff Leadership & Organizational Development

Lead And Develop a Talented Professional Team Through

Coaching, mentoring, and regular supervision
Thoughtful onboarding, employee development, and continuous learning opportunities
Performance management and annual review processes
Building a culture where reflection, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement are expected and supported
The Executive Director supervises the Administration and Operations Team (currently five employees) and contracted personnel, including security and catering staff.

Administration & Operations

Provide Executive Oversight For The Synagogue's Administrative Functions, Including

Financial stewardship and budget management
Facilities and vendor relationships
Human resources
Operational planning
High Holy Days and major congregational events
Life-cycle logistics, including B'nei Mitzvah and funerals
Board and Executive Committee support
Volunteer coordination
Organizational policies and procedures

Qualifications

The strongest candidates will bring:

Four or more years of leadership experience in a nonprofit, synagogue, or other mission-driven organization.
Demonstrated success in leading and developing professional staff.
Experience in fundraising, donor cultivation, grant management, or organizational development.
Strong financial, operational, and organizational management skills.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to build relationships with clergy, staff, volunteers, and lay leaders.
Experience working with volunteer boards and committees.
Understanding of, or enthusiasm for learning about, Reform Jewish life, traditions, and the Jewish calendar.
A collaborative, reflective leader who demonstrates integrity, sound judgment, curiosity, and a commitment to continuous learning and growth.

Don't Meet Every Qualification?

Research consistently shows that many talented candidates, particularly women and historically underrepresented professionals, are less likely to apply unless they meet every listed qualification. If this opportunity excites you and you believe you could thrive in this role, we encourage you to apply.

Compensation & Benefits

Salary:
$120,000–$140,000

Benefits Include

Health benefits
Paid vacation
Professional development opportunities
A supportive and collaborative workplace
The opportunity to partner with visionary clergy, dedicated lay leaders, and an engaged congregation
The chance to help shape the future of one of Northern California's leading Reform Jewish communities

About Congregation Shomrei Torah

Rabbi Jeremy Morrison joined CST in July 2025, beginning an exciting new chapter in our congregation's 50-year history.

Rabbi Morrison envisions CST as a "sanctuary for imperfect practice,"
a place where individuals and families strive toward spiritual, ethical, and communal growth with honesty, curiosity, and humility.

We are a congregation devoted to lifelong learning, for our congregants, clergy, volunteers, and staff alike. We celebrate our successes while continually asking how we can become a more diverse, welcoming, socially conscious, and spiritually vibrant community that helps repair our world through Reform Jewish values.

jobs.title: Executive Director, Enterprise Program Management Office (PMO)
jobs.description:
At Veracyte, we offer exciting career opportunities for those interested in joining a pioneering team that is committed to transforming cancer care for patients across the globe. Working at Veracyte enables our employees to not only make a meaningful impact on the lives of patients, but to also learn and grow within a purpose driven environment. This is what we call the Veracyte way – it’s about how we work together, guided by our values, to give clinicians the insights they need to help patients make life-changing decisions.

Our Values

We Seek A Better Way: We pursue bold ideas, embrace complexity, and keep pushing forward.
We Make It Happen: We act with urgency, deliver with excellence, and always find a way.
We Are Stronger Together: We engage with empathy, align around what's best for Veracyte, and celebrate as one team.
We Care Deeply: We show up with integrity, kindness, and respect for one another.

The Position

Veracyte is seeking an Executive Director, Enterprise Program Management Office (PMO) to play a central role in helping us fulfill our mission to transform cancer care with breakthrough molecular diagnostics and AI insights for patients and providers worldwide, leveraging our whole transcriptome and whole genome multi-omics platform. Reporting directly to the Chief Development and Technology Officer, this leader will help accelerate Veracyte’s growth, technical capabilities, and expanding product offerings in key cancer indications by strengthening how we advance strategic initiatives from concept through feasibility, development, and launch. This is a highly visible, high-impact role for a collaborative and trusted leader who can build a next-generation Product Development Process (PDP) that brings rigor, speed, accountability, and clear decision-making to our most important work while reflecting Veracyte’s values of innovation, collaboration, and making it happen.

This position is a hybrid role based out of our San Diego office.

What You’ll Do

Transform Veracyte’s Product Development Process (PDP) into a scalable operating model for advancing initiatives from concept through launch.
Lead enterprise portfolio governance, including intake, prioritization, stage gates, sequencing, escalations, and executive trade-off decisions.
Facilitate monthly executive updates that create shared visibility, thoughtful decisions, and timely resolution of risks, dependencies, and blockers.
Lead quarterly capacity planning to align priorities, resources, timelines, and trade-offs.
Own annual program intake process and portfolio alignment accounting for budget, capacity, business value, and strategic fit.
Standardize program cadence, templates, dashboards, decision records, timelines, risk tracking, and action management.
Strengthen timeline reliability, milestone integrity, critical-path focus, and launch excellence
Define portfolio KPIs for velocity, operational readiness, resource use, and value realization
Serve as a trusted partner across Product, R&D, Operations, Bioinformatics, Software, Finance, Quality, Regulatory, Legal, Commercial, and Market Access.
Prepare clear executive and Board communications, including decision briefs, portfolio updates, risk summaries, and program investment landscape.
Build and lead a high-performing PMO team including hiring, career development, best practices, and a clear vision for the function.

Who You Are

Executive-level PMO, product portfolio management (PPM), or product governance leadership in complex, regulated environments.
Deep expertise in product development, stage-gate governance, portfolio prioritization, resource planning, risk management, and launch readiness.
Proven ability to transform fragmented practices into standardized, scalable, data-driven execution systems.
Strong business acumen, with the ability to connect investment, resources, capacity, trade-offs, and ROI.
Exceptional executive communication skills for senior leadership and development teams alike
Independent judgment and influence to surface risks, resolve blockers, clarify decisions, and help teams move forward.
Strategic thinker who can design operating models while diving into details and solving problems when execution requires it.
Passion for building a PMO center of excellence through coaching, upskilling, practical standards, and shared best practices.
Urgency balanced with quality, collaboration, and patient impact, using agile product development methods to improve speed and transparency.
A personable leadership style grounded in clarity, coaching, accountability, humility, and trust.

Preferred Qualifications

13+ years in program management, portfolio management, product development, or related leadership roles, including 8+ years leading teams or enterprise programs.
Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, engineering, business, or related field required; advanced degree, MBA, or program/portfolio certification preferred.
Experience in diagnostics, life sciences, medtech, biotech, pharmaceutical, or other regulated product environments.
Balancing clinical, regulatory, quality, laboratory, tech, and commercial launch dependencies.
Experience integrating PDP, quality management system (QMS), software development lifecycle (SDLC), and portfolio-management tools.
Ability to build governance mechanisms, dashboards, and cadences that improve transparency and decision quality.
Experience with portfolio analytics, scenario planning, capacity modeling, and value-based prioritization.
Experience implementing enterprise project tools, dashboards, and reporting systems as a reliable source of truth.
Change-management experience rolling out new ways of working.
Aptitude with modern AI tools to automate routine work, improve reporting, and increase PMO productivity.

For candidates based in our San Diego office
, the salary range is $264,000 - $293,000.

The final salary offered to a successful candidate will be dependent on several factors that may include but are not limited to years of experience, skillset, geographic location, industry, education, etc. Base pay is one part of the Total Package that is provided to compensate and recognize employees for their work, and this role may be eligible for additional discretionary bonuses/incentives, and restricted stock units.

Pay range

$264,000—$293,000 USD

What We Can Offer You

Veracyte is a growing company that offers significant career opportunities if you are curious, driven, patient-oriented and aspire to help us build a great company. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, and are committed to fostering an inclusive workforce, where diverse backgrounds are represented, engaged, and empowered to drive innovative ideas and decisions. We are thrilled to be recognized as a 2024 Certified™ Great Place to Work® in both the US and Israel - a testament to our dynamic, inclusive, and inspiring workplace where passion meets purpose.

About Veracyte

Veracyte (Nasdaq: VCYT) is a global diagnostics company whose vision is to transform cancer care for patients all over the world. We empower clinicians with the high-value insights they need to guide and assure patients at pivotal moments in the race to diagnose and treat cancer. Our Veracyte Diagnostics Platform delivers high-performing cancer tests that are fueled by broad genomic and clinical data, deep bioinformatic and AI capabilities, and a powerful evidence-generation engine, which ultimately drives durable reimbursement and guideline inclusion for our tests, along with new insights to support continued innovation and pipeline development. For more information, please visit www.veracyte.com or follow us on LinkedIn or X (Twitter).

Description

ABOUT CONGREGATION RODEPH SHOLOM

Congregation Rodeph Sholom (CRS) is a large dynamic Reform synagogue at the heart of Manhattan’s Upper West Side and has a strong 185-year history. We are a community for all who enter our doors and our members represent the vibrant diversity of New York’s Jewish landscape. Multi-generational families, interfaith families, lifelong New Yorkers, those new to the city, people pursuing conversion and those exploring Judaism for the first time have all found a home at CRS.

About Working Here

A goal for all clergy and staff is to strive to demonstrate consistent relationship-building across all interactions, recognizing each person and exchange as an opportunity to strengthen trust, collaboration, and connection with congregants and across the organization.

About You

This position requires a self-starter with excellent judgment. The individual must be able to work independently, handle confidential information, prioritize multiple tasks, and have keen attention to detail. The ideal candidate has strong project management skills, excellent organizational skills, is technically savvy, and has strong communication skills.

WORK SCHEDULE

This position requires 4 days in person with 1 possible remote day per week scheduled in coordination with the Executive Director. Team members must be flexible and able to adapt to short-and long-term shifts in their job responsibilities. Working hours are generally 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM (4:00 PM on Fridays); additional hours will be required in the evenings for events related to the Board of Trustees and Annual Meeting.

Responsibilities

This position provides high-level administrative support to the Executive Director.

Manage the Executive Director’s calendar, including creating Doodle polls, scheduling meetings including other staff, and preparing the ED for her upcoming meetings
Draft and proofread correspondence. reports, power point presentations, and other document to lay leaders and vendors
Main administrative point of contact for Trustees
Create reports from Salesforce; responsible for Board of Trustee data and dashboards
Maintain both private and public Board records and relevant documents, ensuring that all necessary information is up-to-date and accessible
Create and maintain Board of Trustees private Group within Salesforce
Coordinate and manage logistics for board meetings, including scheduling, room set-up, preparation of meeting packets and power point decks, ordering food, managing board communications, being on-site on day-of meetings, coordinating A/V support, and drafting minutes for meetings

Assists with Executive Director’s strategic projects; participate in meetings as necessary to collect minutes and action items for ED
Main internal point-person for Annual Meeting
Answer the Executive Director’s phone line
Process invoices and Amex bills in Concur (weekly/monthly)
Ad hoc project assistance for ED and for CFO (as needed)
Manage communication and tasks between ED and Chief Financial Officer

Requirements

Bachelor's degree preferred
1-3 years experience as an executive assistant or in a similar administrative role, preferably in a non-profit environment
Strong knowledge of office management systems including Microsoft Office and Zoom
Skilled in PowerPoint and Excel and knowledge or ability to learn and become skilled in Salesforce
Excellent organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to handle multiple priorities and meet deadlines
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to interact professionally with a variety of stakeholders
Discretion and confidentiality when handling sensitive information
Proactive, self-motivated, and able to work independently with minimal supervision
Experience with financial or budgetary tasks is preferred

Salary & Benefits

Salary range: $63,000-68,000; commensurate with experience
Generous paid time off (e.g., vacation, holidays, sick and personal days, and parental leave)
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance
403(b) retirement plan with up to a 7% matching contribution
Flexible Spending Accounts for commuter, dependent care, and medical expenses.
Short-term disability, long-term disability, and life insurance
AFLAC plans
Gym membership subsidy
Professional development

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
Our client is seeking an exceptional Chief Operating Officer to lead operations for a growing, privately held Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization (CDMO) specializing in nutraceuticals, dietary supplements, and related wellness products. This is a high-impact executive role reporting to the CEO, responsible for driving operational excellence, scaling manufacturing capacity, strengthening customer delivery, and building a high-performing leadership team capable of supporting aggressive growth.
The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced, customer-centric contract manufacturing environment where production schedules and client relationships are tightly linked. Success requires decisive leadership, operational discipline, and the ability to deliver measurable improvements without relying on constant CEO intervention

Key Responsibilities:

• Lead in a true CDMO / contract manufacturing model—managing to customer specifications, timelines, and cost structures rather than a single internal product roadmap.
• Provide overall leadership for complex manufacturing operations, including production, supply chain, planning, maintenance, and operational performance.
• Drive executive decision-making with urgency and confidence, making timely calls and maintaining momentum even without perfect information.
• Establish and enforce operational discipline through clear processes, KPIs, accountability systems, and consistent operating rhythms that eliminate firefighting.
• Build, develop, and lead a high-energy, high-performing operations leadership team focused on rapid and disciplined execution.
• Oversee operations in an FDA-regulated environment, ensuring quality and compliance while maintaining speed; manage customer and third-party audit readiness and responses.
• Tightly integrate Operations with Sales, Account Management, Commercialization, QA/QC, and Finance to ensure seamless customer experience and commercial success.
• Manage both internal production and outsourced manufacturing partners / co-packers, including quality oversight, capacity planning, and margin accountability across models.
• Drive continuous improvement in productivity, capacity utilization, cost, quality, service levels, and on-time delivery.
• Support executive-level transitions and organizational change with strategic clarity and practical execution.

Required Qualifications & Experience:

• Proven track record of executive decision-making and driving results in fast-paced environments without waiting for perfect information.
• Direct experience in a CDMO or contract manufacturing setting where customer relationships and production schedules are inseparable.
• Significant experience leading complex manufacturing operations (production, supply chain, planning, maintenance, and performance management).
• Demonstrated ability to install processes, KPIs, accountability, and operating rhythms that create consistent performance.
• Strong team-building skills combined with high energy and a bias for rapid, high-quality implementation.
• Direct experience operating in an FDA-regulated manufacturing facility, including customer and third-party audit exposure; comfortable balancing quality/compliance constraints with speed.
• Experience with executive-level transitions (either leading them or having a meaningful seat in the room).
• Ability to tightly connect Operations with Sales, Account Management, Commercialization, QA/QC, and Finance.
• Track record managing external manufacturing partners or co-packers alongside internal production, with clear ownership of quality, capacity, and margins.
• Proven continuous improvement results in productivity, capacity, cost, quality, service levels, and on-time delivery.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Significant industry gravitas that immediately elevates the company’s credibility and “Q” rating with customers, partners, and the broader nutraceutical ecosystem.
• Ideally full-time onsite presence; a realistic minimum of 3 days per week onsite is expected.
• Experience in private company environments.

Compensation:
$300,000+

ABOUT NGPF
Next Gen Personal Finance (NGPF) is a nonprofit on a mission to ensure that every U.S. high school student takes a personal finance course before they graduate (Mission 2030). We provide free, high-quality curriculum, professional development, and support to educators and school district partners nationwide, helping them teach students how to manage money and make informed financial decisions.

More than 150,000 educators use NGPF resources, and our market size is expected to triple in the next several years as 20 new states are requiring students to take a personal finance course as a result of our advocacy efforts.

We are a small but mighty team that values collaboration and a shared commitment to expanding access to financial education. Our work is fast-paced, meaningful, and driven by the impact we can have on the next generation.

Our most powerful asset has always been teachers. The next chapter of NGPF's growth depends on organizing our most passionate educators into a national force: presenting at conferences, leading professional development, and advocating for personal finance education in the 20 states that have yet to guarantee the course.

ABOUT THE ROLE
The Manager of the Teacher Ambassador Program will build, develop, and mobilize a national network of NGPF Ambassador teachers: experienced, credible educators who extend NGPF's reach far beyond what our staff of ~22 could accomplish alone. You will identify the right teachers, equip them with training and resources, match them to high-impact opportunities, and celebrate their leadership.

This is a role for a collaborative builder. You will inherit a deep bench of engaged teachers (FinCamp attendees, Fellows, award winners, certification completers), and turn their enthusiasm into a structured, high-performing ambassador program with clear expectations, strong support, and measurable impact.

You will work alongside and report to NGPF’s Director of Teacher Success, but collaborate across the organization.

Your signature project in year one: serving as project manager for the NGPF Teacher Ambassador Conference in Atlanta in March 2027, a ~200-person national gathering that will be the Ambassador program's launch pad.

WHAT YOU'LL DO
Build and develop the Ambassador network

Design the program structure: selection criteria, expectations, tiers, stipends/recognition, and annual cycle
Recruit a strong founding cohort of Ambassador teachers from NGPF's most engaged educators, with attention to geographic coverage (priority for implementation and advocacy states)
Create onboarding, training, and ongoing development materials to help Ambassadors confidently represent NGPF (presentation skills, talking points, advocacy training, media readiness, etc.)
Serve as the primary relationship manager for Ambassadors: regular communication, community building, and recognition

Deploy Ambassadors for impact

Manage a calendar of state and national conferences (JumpStart, CEE, state business/FCS/social studies conferences) and coordinate Ambassador attendance and presentations on behalf of NGPF
Coordinate Ambassador-led professional development in their own districts and neighboring districts, working with our PD team on content and quality
Source and staff panel, media, and speaking opportunities that match Ambassadors' expertise
Support Ambassador participation in state house advocacy (testimony, advocacy days, legislator meetings) in the 20 states without a personal finance guarantee, in coordination with NGPF's advocacy team
Identify new opportunities for or models of Ambassador engagement that advance NGPF’s mission and align with organizational goals
Own end-to-end execution of the inaugural Ambassador conference (March 2027) to set program culture, train the founding Ambassador cohort, and launch the year's Ambassador engagement plan
Collaborate with NGPF’s Directors of Professional Development and Teacher Success on program goals

Lead the Ambassador program like an operator

Track everything: activations, presentations delivered, teachers reached, districts served, advocacy touchpoints
Manage program budget, including travel, stipends, and event costs
Report on program impact and continuously improve based on Ambassador and audience feedback
Identify operational improvements, opportunities to automate, and build repeatable systems to scale what works

WHO YOU'LL WORK WITH
You will report to:
Director of Teacher Success
You will collaborate with:
Professional Development, Teacher Success, Advocacy, and teams across the organization

WHO YOU ARE
5+ years of experience in education, edtech, or nonprofit program management; classroom teaching experience is a strong plus
Proven event or conference project management experience (you have run complex, multi-stakeholder events and sweat the details)
A natural community builder who earns teachers' trust quickly and makes volunteers feel valued
Strong facilitator and communicator, comfortable presenting to educators, administrators, and policymakers
Organized and self-directed; you can manage dozens of simultaneous relationships, deadlines, and travel logistics without dropping balls
Willingness to travel (roughly 15-20%, including some weekends for conferences)
Passion for NGPF's mission of financial education for all students

WHY THIS ROLE
This is a rare chance to build a national program from the ground up at the organization leading the personal finance education movement. You will own a visible, high-impact portfolio, work directly with senior leadership, and develop skills across community building, event management, professional development, and policy advocacy. As the Ambassador program grows, so does this role.

A comprehensive benefits package includes, but is not limited to: health insurance, 401(k) matching contribution, 18 paid vacation days (on top of company-wide holidays), 12 weeks of paid parental leave, and various additional benefits.

This role is open to candidates across the United States. NGPF has an office in Burlingame, CA. If you are located within 50 miles of Burlingame, you will be expected to work in a hybrid capacity with two in-office days per week. Candidates outside of this area will work fully remote.

The Managing Director owns the end-to-end operation of IDEA Florida's student information system (FOCUS), drives a culture of data integrity across all six Florida campuses, and serves as the primary authority on all requirements under Florida's Comprehensive Management Information System (CMIS) and the Automated Student Attendance Recordkeeping System (ATDM). This leader partners closely with school principals, the Florida Executive Director, and IPS's national finance and operations teams to ensure that student data directly supports enrollment growth, FTE funding accuracy, and compliance with all state and federal regulatory requirements.

Supervisory Responsibilities: This role will:

Directly supervises MIS Coordinators/Specialists at each Florida campus
Provide functional oversight of campus-level data entry staff responsible for FOCUS system inputs
Partner with the IPS HR Director on hiring, onboarding, and performance management for direct reports

Location: This is a full-time (remote/on-site) position based in Florida, with preference given to candidates who live in Jacksonville, Tampa or Lakeland, or who are willing to relocate.

Travel Expectations: Regular travel to all IDEA Florida campuses (in Jacksonville, Lakeland and Tampa) to support data quality reviews, staff training, and compliance preparation. An additional 10% of travel time will include attendance at FDOE trainings, stakeholder meetings, and relevant conferences

What You’ll Do – Essential Duties And Accountabilities

State Reporting and Regulatory Compliance

Own and manage all Florida state reporting submissions through FOCUS, including all FDOE survey windows (Surveys 1–5) and end-of-year reporting
Ensure full compliance with Florida's Comprehensive Management Information System (CMIS) requirements, including all automated student attendance recordkeeping requirements under Rule 6A-1.044(3), FAC and Section 1003.23, Florida Statutes
Maintain complete, accurate, and audit-ready student attendance records at both the school and district level — including daily PK–12 records (ESE 950/ESE 955) and period-by-period records for grades 9–12 (ESE 953, ESE 954, ESE 956, ESE 981)
Manage all student entry, re-entry, and withdrawal coding in FOCUS, ensuring accurate use of applicable codes (DNE, W-codes, R-codes) consistent with FDOE requirements
Coordinate FTE (Full-Time Equivalent) survey submissions and support FTE audit preparation — ensuring that all attendance records, membership data, and supporting documentation are complete and accessible for a three-year audit window
Ensure accurate and timely tracking and reporting of all special student populations, including: Hospital/Homebound students, Virtual instruction students, ESE students in resource/pullout classes, Early admission and dual enrollment students, Year-round and intersession enrollment
Monitor and enforce adherence to FDOE attendance definitions and procedures — including proper use of excused/unexcused absence codes, tardy recording, and compulsory attendance law requirements
Maintain full compliance with data privacy regulations applicable to Florida public charter schools, including FERPA, CCPA, and HIPAA as applicable

Student Information System (FOCUS) Management

Serve as the organizational lead and primary system administrator for FOCUS across all IDEA Florida campuses
Ensure FOCUS is configured, maintained, and continuously improved to meet all FDOE reporting requirements and IDEA Florida operational needs
Develop and enforce system-wide data entry standards, audit procedures, and user access protocols across all six campuses
Establish and maintain electronic recordkeeping procedures that comply with Rule 6A-1.044(2), FAC — including audit log maintenance, sign-on indicators, backup and redundancy protocols, and daily change logging
Coordinate with FOCUS vendor on system updates, issue resolution, data interoperability needs, and customization aligned with Florida-specific requirements
Lead regular data audits in FOCUS to proactively identify and correct errors prior to state reporting windows
Develop and maintain documentation, standard operating procedures, training materials, and user guides for all FOCUS workflows

Data Quality And Integrity

Build and sustain a culture of data accuracy across all Florida campuses — ensuring that school staff understand and own their role in the data pipeline
Design and implement a systematic data quality review cycle aligned to FDOE survey calendars, FTE count periods, and IDEA's internal enrollment reporting cadences
Establish 100% on-time submission as the standard for all state and district reporting deadlines
Partner with school principals and campus MIS staff to identify root causes of data errors and implement corrective training and process improvements
Analyze enrollment, attendance, and withdrawal trends to surface insights relevant to IDEA Florida's student persistence and enrollment goals

Cross Functional Partnership & Leadership

Serve as the primary liaison between IDEA Florida and FDOE on all matters related to student data, MIS reporting, and compliance
Partner with the IPS VP of Finance and Controller to ensure FTE revenue projections are grounded in accurate enrollment and attendance data
Collaborate with IPS's national HR team to maintain accurate employee data in systems that intersect with state reporting
Support the Florida Executive Director with data and analysis for board reporting, fiduciary oversight, and strategic planning
Coordinate with IPS's national IST/technology leadership on system infrastructure, data security, and any technology needs related to MIS operations
Represent IDEA Florida in PAEC (Panhandle Area Educational Consortium) and other Florida charter/district MIS professional communities, staying current on changes to FDOE requirements and best practices

Training and Organizational Capacity

Design and deliver ongoing training programs for campus MIS staff, school administrators, and teachers on FOCUS data entry, attendance procedures, and state reporting requirements
Ensure all campus staff responsible for attendance recordkeeping understand and follow FDOE procedures — including proper use of electronic attendance systems, sign-on requirements, and audit trail maintenance
Build internal MIS capacity so that IDEA Florida is not reliant on any single person for state reporting continuity

What You Will Bring – Required Knowledge & Skills

Deep expertise in Florida K-12 education data systems and FDOE state reporting requirements, including FTE surveys, CMIS/ATDM compliance, and attendance recordkeeping under Florida Statutes and State Board of Education Rules
Demonstrated experience administering or leading operations in a student information system — FOCUS experience strongly preferred; experience with other Florida-compliant SIS platforms (Skyward, PowerSchool, Infinite Campus) considered
Fluency in Florida attendance definitions, codes, and procedures: daily attendance (PK-12), period-by-period (9-12), entry/withdrawal/re-entry coding, DNE procedures, FTE audit requirements, Hospital/Homebound, Virtual School, and Intersession recordkeeping
Strong analytical skills — able to identify data patterns, audit for errors, and communicate data findings clearly to non-technical audiences including school leaders and executives
Excellent project management skills — able to manage multiple simultaneous deadlines including state survey windows, FTE submissions, and internal reporting calendars
Strong interpersonal and communication skills — able to build relationships with school principals, campus staff, FDOE contacts, and IPS leadership
Familiarity with applicable data privacy regulations (FERPA, CCPA, HIPAA) in the context of K-12 student data

Required Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree required; field of study in Education, Information Systems, Data Analytics, Business, or a related field preferred
Advanced degree or relevant Florida education data certifications a plus
5+ years of experience in K-12 education data management, MIS, or state reporting — with at least 3 years in a Florida public school district or charter management organization
Prior supervisory or team leadership experience required
Experience managing data compliance in a multi-site or multi-campus environment strongly preferred
Prior experience working with or for Florida charter schools a plus

Salaries for people entering this role typically fall between $114,100 and $144,600, commensurate with relevant experience and qualifications and in alignment with internal equity. This role is also eligible for performance pay based on organizational performance and goal attainment.

IDEA Florida currently operates six schools serving approximately 5,000 students. IPS Enterprises, Inc. is the management company for all IDEA Public Schools operating outside of Texas. About the National Aviary

The National Aviary is America’s only independent indoor nonprofit zoo dedicated exclusively to birds. Located in West Park on Pittsburgh’s historic North Side, the National Aviary is home to more than 500 birds representing more than 150 species from around the world, many of them threatened or endangered in the wild. 

The National Aviary’s large walk-through habitats create an experience unlike any other – an intimate, up-close immersive experience between visitors and free-flying birds, including opportunities to hand-feed and meet many species rarely found in zoos anywhere else in the world.

As an environmental organization composed of educators, conservationists and researchers, the National Aviary’s goals are many. The National Aviary aims to provide outstanding education programming for varied audiences; present the highest quality family recreational experience that a zoological institution can offer; save endangered species by preserving natural habitats; continue endangered bird breeding programs and conduct meaningful avian research; engender a sincere appreciation of nature and a respect for natural law; and instill a conservation ethic that teaches our immense responsibility as stewards of the planet.

We provide free, high-quality curriculum, professional development, and support to educators and school district partners nationwide, helping them teach students how to manage money and make informed financial decisions.

More than 150,000 educators use NGPF resources, and our market size is expected to triple in the next several years as 20 new states are requiring students to take a personal finance course as a result of our advocacy efforts.

We are a small but mighty team that values collaboration and a shared commitment to expanding access to financial education. Our work is fast-paced, meaningful, and driven by the impact we can have on the next generation.

Our most powerful asset has always been teachers. The next chapter of NGPF's growth depends on organizing our most passionate educators into a national force: presenting at conferences, leading professional development, and advocating for personal finance education in the 20 states that have yet to guarantee the course.

ABOUT THE ROLE
The Manager of the Teacher Ambassador Program will build, develop, and mobilize a national network of NGPF Ambassador teachers: experienced, credible educators who extend NGPF's reach far beyond what our staff of ~22 could accomplish alone. You will identify the right teachers, equip them with training and resources, match them to high-impact opportunities, and celebrate their leadership.

This is a role for a collaborative builder. You will inherit a deep bench of engaged teachers (FinCamp attendees, Fellows, award winners, certification completers), and turn their enthusiasm into a structured, high-performing ambassador program with clear expectations, strong support, and measurable impact.

You will work alongside and report to NGPF’s Director of Teacher Success, but collaborate across the organization.

Your signature project in year one: serving as project manager for the NGPF Teacher Ambassador Conference in Atlanta in March 2027, a ~200-person national gathering that will be the Ambassador program's launch pad.

WHAT YOU'LL DO
Build and develop the Ambassador network

Design the program structure: selection criteria, expectations, tiers, stipends/recognition, and annual cycle
Recruit a strong founding cohort of Ambassador teachers from NGPF's most engaged educators, with attention to geographic coverage (priority for implementation and advocacy states)
Create onboarding, training, and ongoing development materials to help Ambassadors confidently represent NGPF (presentation skills, talking points, advocacy training, media readiness, etc.)
Serve as the primary relationship manager for Ambassadors: regular communication, community building, and recognition

Deploy Ambassadors for impact

Manage a calendar of state and national conferences (JumpStart, CEE, state business/FCS/social studies conferences) and coordinate Ambassador attendance and presentations on behalf of NGPF
Coordinate Ambassador-led professional development in their own districts and neighboring districts, working with our PD team on content and quality
Source and staff panel, media, and speaking opportunities that match Ambassadors' expertise
Support Ambassador participation in state house advocacy (testimony, advocacy days, legislator meetings) in the 20 states without a personal finance guarantee, in coordination with NGPF's advocacy team
Identify new opportunities for or models of Ambassador engagement that advance NGPF’s mission and align with organizational goals
Own end-to-end execution of the inaugural Ambassador conference (March 2027) to set program culture, train the founding Ambassador cohort, and launch the year's Ambassador engagement plan
Collaborate with NGPF’s Directors of Professional Development and Teacher Success on program goals

Lead the Ambassador program like an operator

Track everything: activations, presentations delivered, teachers reached, districts served, advocacy touchpoints
Manage program budget, including travel, stipends, and event costs
Report on program impact and continuously improve based on Ambassador and audience feedback
Identify operational improvements, opportunities to automate, and build repeatable systems to scale what works

WHO YOU'LL WORK WITH
You will report to:
Director of Teacher Success
You will collaborate with:
Professional Development, Teacher Success, Advocacy, and teams across the organization

WHO YOU ARE
5+ years of experience in education, edtech, or nonprofit program management; classroom teaching experience is a strong plus
Proven event or conference project management experience (you have run complex, multi-stakeholder events and sweat the details)
A natural community builder who earns teachers' trust quickly and makes volunteers feel valued
Strong facilitator and communicator, comfortable presenting to educators, administrators, and policymakers
Organized and self-directed; you can manage dozens of simultaneous relationships, deadlines, and travel logistics without dropping balls
Willingness to travel (roughly 15-20%, including some weekends for conferences)
Passion for NGPF's mission of financial education for all students

WHY THIS ROLE
This is a rare chance to build a national program from the ground up at the organization leading the personal finance education movement. You will own a visible, high-impact portfolio, work directly with senior leadership, and develop skills across community building, event management, professional development, and policy advocacy. As the Ambassador program grows, so does this role.

JOB DETAILS
Salary:
$100K - $115K, commensurate with experience
Benefits:
A comprehensive benefits package includes, but is not limited to: health insurance, 401(k) matching contribution, 18 paid vacation days (on top of company-wide holidays), 12 weeks of paid parental leave, and various additional benefits.
Job location:
This role is open to candidates across the United States. NGPF has an office in Burlingame, CA. If you are located within 50 miles of Burlingame, you will be expected to work in a hybrid capacity with two in-office days per week. Candidates outside of this area will work fully remote.
Travel:
Roughly 15-20%, including some weekends for conferences
Target start date:
October 1st, 2026

Complete application form here: https://www.ngpf.org/teacher-ambassador-program-manager/

SurgiSTUD develops high-fidelity, biomechanically accurate surgical training models that transform the way orthopedic surgeons and medical device companies train and innovate. As a growing leader in surgical training technology, we are seeking a Chief Development Officer to define where the company competes, what it builds next, and which partnerships carry it forward.  

Position Summary

The Chief Development Officer is responsible for the growth strategy of the organization and for the external relationships that support it. The position establishes where the company competes, which products and capabilities are developed next, and which partnerships are pursued.  
The Chief Development Officer serves as a senior representative of the organization to external stakeholders and holds primary accountability for revenue growth and long-term commercial positioning. Growth Strategy

Description

Managing Director of Management Information Systems (MIS)

Role Mission: The Managing Director of Management Information Systems (MIS) leads all student data management, state compliance reporting, and information systems strategy for IDEA Public Schools' Florida region. This role is the linchpin between our schools, the Florida Department of Education (FDOE), and our internal teams — ensuring that every piece of student data is accurate, compliant, timely, and actionable.

The Managing Director owns the end-to-end operation of IDEA Florida's student information system (FOCUS), drives a culture of data integrity across all six Florida campuses, and serves as the primary authority on all requirements under Florida's Comprehensive Management Information System (CMIS) and the Automated Student Attendance Recordkeeping System (ATDM). This leader partners closely with school principals, the Florida Executive Director, and IPS's national finance and operations teams to ensure that student data directly supports enrollment growth, FTE funding accuracy, and compliance with all state and federal regulatory requirements.

Supervisory Responsibilities: This role will:

Directly supervises MIS Coordinators/Specialists at each Florida campus
Provide functional oversight of campus-level data entry staff responsible for FOCUS system inputs
Partner with the IPS HR Director on hiring, onboarding, and performance management for direct reports

Location: This is a full-time (remote/on-site) position based in Florida, with preference given to candidates who live in Jacksonville, Tampa or Lakeland, or who are willing to relocate.

Travel Expectations: Regular travel to all IDEA Florida campuses (in Jacksonville, Lakeland and Tampa) to support data quality reviews, staff training, and compliance preparation. An additional 10% of travel time will include attendance at FDOE trainings, stakeholder meetings, and relevant conferences

What You’ll Do – Essential Duties And Accountabilities

State Reporting and Regulatory Compliance

Own and manage all Florida state reporting submissions through FOCUS, including all FDOE survey windows (Surveys 1–5) and end-of-year reporting
Ensure full compliance with Florida's Comprehensive Management Information System (CMIS) requirements, including all automated student attendance recordkeeping requirements under Rule 6A-1.044(3), FAC and Section 1003.23, Florida Statutes
Maintain complete, accurate, and audit-ready student attendance records at both the school and district level — including daily PK–12 records (ESE 950/ESE 955) and period-by-period records for grades 9–12 (ESE 953, ESE 954, ESE 956, ESE 981)
Manage all student entry, re-entry, and withdrawal coding in FOCUS, ensuring accurate use of applicable codes (DNE, W-codes, R-codes) consistent with FDOE requirements
Coordinate FTE (Full-Time Equivalent) survey submissions and support FTE audit preparation — ensuring that all attendance records, membership data, and supporting documentation are complete and accessible for a three-year audit window
Ensure accurate and timely tracking and reporting of all special student populations, including: Hospital/Homebound students, Virtual instruction students, ESE students in resource/pullout classes, Early admission and dual enrollment students, Year-round and intersession enrollment
Monitor and enforce adherence to FDOE attendance definitions and procedures — including proper use of excused/unexcused absence codes, tardy recording, and compulsory attendance law requirements
Maintain full compliance with data privacy regulations applicable to Florida public charter schools, including FERPA, CCPA, and HIPAA as applicable

Student Information System (FOCUS) Management

Serve as the organizational lead and primary system administrator for FOCUS across all IDEA Florida campuses
Ensure FOCUS is configured, maintained, and continuously improved to meet all FDOE reporting requirements and IDEA Florida operational needs
Develop and enforce system-wide data entry standards, audit procedures, and user access protocols across all six campuses
Establish and maintain electronic recordkeeping procedures that comply with Rule 6A-1.044(2), FAC — including audit log maintenance, sign-on indicators, backup and redundancy protocols, and daily change logging
Coordinate with FOCUS vendor on system updates, issue resolution, data interoperability needs, and customization aligned with Florida-specific requirements
Lead regular data audits in FOCUS to proactively identify and correct errors prior to state reporting windows
Develop and maintain documentation, standard operating procedures, training materials, and user guides for all FOCUS workflows

Data Quality And Integrity

Build and sustain a culture of data accuracy across all Florida campuses — ensuring that school staff understand and own their role in the data pipeline
Design and implement a systematic data quality review cycle aligned to FDOE survey calendars, FTE count periods, and IDEA's internal enrollment reporting cadences
Establish 100% on-time submission as the standard for all state and district reporting deadlines
Partner with school principals and campus MIS staff to identify root causes of data errors and implement corrective training and process improvements
Analyze enrollment, attendance, and withdrawal trends to surface insights relevant to IDEA Florida's student persistence and enrollment goals

Cross Functional Partnership & Leadership

Serve as the primary liaison between IDEA Florida and FDOE on all matters related to student data, MIS reporting, and compliance
Partner with the IPS VP of Finance and Controller to ensure FTE revenue projections are grounded in accurate enrollment and attendance data
Collaborate with IPS's national HR team to maintain accurate employee data in systems that intersect with state reporting
Support the Florida Executive Director with data and analysis for board reporting, fiduciary oversight, and strategic planning
Coordinate with IPS's national IST/technology leadership on system infrastructure, data security, and any technology needs related to MIS operations
Represent IDEA Florida in PAEC (Panhandle Area Educational Consortium) and other Florida charter/district MIS professional communities, staying current on changes to FDOE requirements and best practices

Training and Organizational Capacity

Design and deliver ongoing training programs for campus MIS staff, school administrators, and teachers on FOCUS data entry, attendance procedures, and state reporting requirements
Ensure all campus staff responsible for attendance recordkeeping understand and follow FDOE procedures — including proper use of electronic attendance systems, sign-on requirements, and audit trail maintenance
Build internal MIS capacity so that IDEA Florida is not reliant on any single person for state reporting continuity

What You Will Bring – Required Knowledge & Skills

Deep expertise in Florida K-12 education data systems and FDOE state reporting requirements, including FTE surveys, CMIS/ATDM compliance, and attendance recordkeeping under Florida Statutes and State Board of Education Rules
Demonstrated experience administering or leading operations in a student information system — FOCUS experience strongly preferred; experience with other Florida-compliant SIS platforms (Skyward, PowerSchool, Infinite Campus) considered
Fluency in Florida attendance definitions, codes, and procedures: daily attendance (PK-12), period-by-period (9-12), entry/withdrawal/re-entry coding, DNE procedures, FTE audit requirements, Hospital/Homebound, Virtual School, and Intersession recordkeeping
Strong analytical skills — able to identify data patterns, audit for errors, and communicate data findings clearly to non-technical audiences including school leaders and executives
Excellent project management skills — able to manage multiple simultaneous deadlines including state survey windows, FTE submissions, and internal reporting calendars
Strong interpersonal and communication skills — able to build relationships with school principals, campus staff, FDOE contacts, and IPS leadership
Familiarity with applicable data privacy regulations (FERPA, CCPA, HIPAA) in the context of K-12 student data

Required Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree required; field of study in Education, Information Systems, Data Analytics, Business, or a related field preferred
Advanced degree or relevant Florida education data certifications a plus
5+ years of experience in K-12 education data management, MIS, or state reporting — with at least 3 years in a Florida public school district or charter management organization
Prior supervisory or team leadership experience required
Experience managing data compliance in a multi-site or multi-campus environment strongly preferred
Prior experience working with or for Florida charter schools a plus

What We Offer

Compensation & Benefits:

Salaries for people entering this role typically fall between $114,100 and $144,600, commensurate with relevant experience and qualifications and in alignment with internal equity. This role is also eligible for performance pay based on organizational performance and goal attainment.

Additionally, we offer medical, dental, and vision plans, disability, life insurance, parenting benefits, flexible spending account options, generous vacation time, referral bonuses, professional development, and a 403(b) plan. You can find more information about our benefits at https://ideapublicschools.org/careers/benefits/.

 IDEA may offer a relocation stipend to defray the cost of moving for this role, if applicable.

About IDEA Florida

IDEA Florida currently operates six schools serving approximately 5,000 students. IPS Enterprises, Inc. is the management company for all IDEA Public Schools operating outside of Texas. The Managing Director of MIS reports to the Florida Executive Director and works closely with the IPS national executive team. IDEA Florida is in an active growth phase, with a goal of reaching approximately 7,000 students over the next 2–3 years — making accurate enrollment data and FTE compliance foundational to the organization's financial sustainability and mission.

About the National Aviary

The National Aviary is America’s only independent indoor nonprofit zoo dedicated exclusively to birds. Located in West Park on Pittsburgh’s historic North Side, the National Aviary is home to more than 500 birds representing more than 150 species from around the world, many of them threatened or endangered in the wild. 

The National Aviary’s large walk-through habitats create an experience unlike any other – an intimate, up-close immersive experience between visitors and free-flying birds, including opportunities to hand-feed and meet many species rarely found in zoos anywhere else in the world.

As an environmental organization composed of educators, conservationists and researchers, the National Aviary’s goals are many. The National Aviary aims to provide outstanding education programming for varied audiences; present the highest quality family recreational experience that a zoological institution can offer; save endangered species by preserving natural habitats; continue endangered bird breeding programs and conduct meaningful avian research; engender a sincere appreciation of nature and a respect for natural law; and instill a conservation ethic that teaches our immense responsibility as stewards of the planet.

Role Description

The Director of Communications leads the National Aviary’s organization-wide communications strategy to build awareness, strengthen and protect the organization’s reputation, and advance its leadership in animal care, avian medicine, conservation, education, and guest engagement. This position is responsible for media relations, institutional storytelling, issues and crisis communications, executive communications, and other high-profile communications that require sound judgment, a clear organizational voice, and close coordination across departments.

The Director of Communications supervises communications staff, manages public relations agency and vendor relationships, and serves as a senior communications advisor to leadership. This position works closely with the Senior Director of External Relations, Executive Director, Director of Marketing, Philanthropy team, subject-matter experts, and colleagues throughout the organization.

Communications Strategy and Organizational Storytelling

Executes an organization-wide communications strategy aligned with the National Aviary’s strategic priorities, brand position, and annual goals.
Coordinates institutional storytelling that communicates the National Aviary’s impact in conservation, avian medicine, education, animal care, community engagement, and guest experience within larger marketing aims and initiatives for seamless messaging.
Oversees long-form storytelling initiatives and editorial publications, including research-focused communications, organizational newsletters, native advertising content, and other mission-driven publications.
Identifies high-value stories and opportunities that advance organizational reputation, determining key messages, audiences, spokespersons, and communications approaches in conjunction with marketing directives, organizational aims, and mission-driven expectations.
Translates complex scientific, veterinary, conservation, and programmatic information into clear, accurate, and engaging public communications.

Media Relations and Thought Leadership

Develops and executes proactive and reactive media relations strategies that increase positive awareness and build organizational reputation.
Oversees creation of media materials, including press releases, advisories, pitches, talking points, and supporting content.
Maintains media relationships, manages inquiries, and coordinates interviews, media events, and spokesperson preparation.
Positions National Aviary experts as trusted resources and thought leaders while monitoring coverage and measuring results.

Issues Management and Crisis Communication

Leads communications planning and response for emerging issues, sensitive matters, and crisis situations in coordination with organizational leadership.
Develops a crisis communication plan.
Maintains crisis communications protocols, messaging resources, media procedures, and spokesperson preparation efforts.
Monitors developments that may affect the National Aviary’s reputation and recommends appropriate communications strategies.
Develops timely statements, key messages, guidance materials, and stakeholder communications during rapidly evolving situations.

Executive and Internal Communications

Collaborates with the Director of Marketing to align institutional storytelling with marketing campaigns.
Supports organization-wide communications related to major initiatives, operational changes, emergencies, and significant announcements.
Partners with Philanthropy and External Relations to develop compelling content for donors, partners, and community stakeholders.
Ensures consistency, accuracy, and effectiveness of messaging across internal and external audiences.

Content Leadership and Cross-Departmental Collaboration

Leads editorial planning for major stories, announcements, publications, and communications priorities across the organization.
Collaborates with the Director of Marketing to align institutional storytelling with campaigns.
Develops and reviews content for digital channels, major organizational news, executive communications, and reputation-related initiatives.
Partners with creative staff, program experts, and external organizations to strengthen storytelling and advance communications goals.

Directs external communications agencies, consultants, and vendors, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and expectations.
Manages communications budgets, establishes performance measures, and evaluates results to strengthen strategy and effectiveness.
Monitors communications trends and best practices while ensuring compliance with National Aviary policies, protocols, and visitor engagement standards.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

OTHER DUTIES

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

The Director of Communications supervises the Assistant Manager, Content and Communications and directs the work of public relations agencies, consultants, and communications vendors.

Exceptional writing, editing, verbal communication, and storytelling skills with the ability to engage diverse audiences.

• Identify and establish manufacturing and supply partnerships that support Hyper Solutions’ growth plans.

The Role

The Director of Communications & Member Engagement is the Chamber's Integrator: the person who makes sure operations, billing/accounting hygiene, and member experience are excellent every single day. This role owns member retention, marketing/communications, and the financial housekeeping of the organization.

What You'll Own

Member Retention & Engagement: You'll be the friendly, familiar voice members hear on renewals and past-due accounts, and the go-to person for members who need a little extra attention. Goal: keep member dues revenue retention at 90% or higher.
Billing & Collections: Handle invoicing, payment processing, and accounts receivable follow-up so no member invoice ages past 90 days, looping in the President early on anything at risk.
Social Media: Lead our social media strategy and content calendar across Facebook, Instagram, and whatever's next, grow our following and engagement year over year, and be our unofficial event photographer.
Marketing & Communications: Own the e-newsletters and emails, member spotlights, and website content.
CRM & Data Integrity: Keep our CRM (ChamberMaster or successor) as the single source of truth for members, invoices, events, and committees, and pull together monthly reporting for the President and Board.
Office & Board Administration: Prepare and distribute board meeting minutes, keep the front desk and office running smoothly, coordinate conference room and AV scheduling, and support our quarterly Member Orientation meetings.
Event Coordination: Help bring our signature events to life, ribbon cuttings, networking events, the Annual Awards Banquet, the Chairman's Memorial Golf Tournament, and the Accelerate Learning Series, working alongside the President and our committees.
Cross-Team Collaboration: Partner with other team members so new members get a warm, seamless welcome.
Other Duties: As assigned.

What You'll Bring

Education: A bachelor's degree in marketing, communications, business, or a related field is preferred, but we're just as interested in equivalent hands-on experience.
Experience: 1-3 years in office or operations management, marketing, communications, or nonprofit/association administration.
Financial Know-How: Comfort with accounts receivable, invoicing, and basic bookkeeping.
Marketing Chops: Experience with growing and managing social media, email marketing, or content programs. Comfortable reading and reporting on the numbers behind them.
Technical Skills: Exceptional Microsoft Suite skills are required. Familiarity with Adobe, Canva, Claude AI or ChatGPT. Experience with a CRM or database platform would be a plus.
Communication: Excellent written and verbal skills, you're comfortable representing the Chamber out in the community, and you handle past-due balances with warmth and tact.
Leadership Potential: You can organize, plan, and run projects on your own. Self-starter who operates with a sense of urgency.
Local Knowledge: Familiarity with Searcy and the local business community, you'll field frequent calls from members and residents needing information or connections.

Please send resume and cover letter to tcathey@searcychamber.com.

Full time, exempt. $44,000-$48,000 depending on experience.
